subject: general
question: The correct sign conventions for focal length (f) and radius of curvature (R) for the formation of images by spherical mirrors is:

options.text: for convex mirror f is negative, R is negative
for concave mirror f is negative, R is negative
for convex mirror f is negative, R is positive
for concave mirror f is positive, R is negative

solution:
The correct answer is **f**__**or **concave mirror f is negative, R is negative__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When dealing with spherical mirrors, a consistent set of sign conventions is crucial for accurate calculations and understanding of image formation. These conventions help determine the nature (real/virtual, erect/inverted), size, and position of the image. 
 
• **Sign Conventions:**
 
 
• Object Distance (u):
 
• Negative: When the object is placed in front of the mirror (the usual case).
 
• Positive: When the object is placed behind the mirror (rarely encountered).
 
• Image Distance (v):
 
• Positive: When the image is formed in front of the mirror (real image).
 
• Negative: When the image is formed behind the mirror (virtual image).
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• Positive: For concave mirrors.
 
• Negative: For convex mirrors.
 
• Radius of Curvature (R):
 
• Positive: For concave mirrors.
 
• Negative: For convex mirrors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relationship Between Focal Length and Radius of Curvature:**

 
 
• The focal length (f) of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature (R) by the following equation:
 
• f = R/2 
 
• Significance of Sign Conventions:
 
• Accurate Calculations: By adhering to these sign conventions, you can correctly apply the mirror formula (1/f = 1/v + 1/u) and magnification formula (m = -v/u) to determine the image characteristics.
 
• Understanding Image Formation: The signs of image distance and magnification provide valuable information about the nature of the image (real/virtual, erect/inverted). 
 
• Consistency: Consistent use of sign conventions ensures that calculations are accurate and reliable, regardless of the type of mirror or the object's position.
